definitions.explanation: The quality of food or drink as perceived by the palate. A more refined or literary term than simply {味|あじ}.
An intangible quality of depth, elegance, or appeal in things like art, scenery, experiences, or craftsmanship. Suggests something that becomes more appreciated the more one engages with it.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}は{深|ふか}い{味|あじ}わいがある。
examples.english: This dish has a deep flavor.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}の{味|あじ}わいを{楽|たの}しむ。
{手作|てづく}りの{器|うつわ}には{独特|どくとく}の{味|あじ}わいがある。
examples.english: Handmade pottery has a unique charm.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{町並|まちな}みには{時代|じだい}の{味|あじ}わいが{感|かん}じられる。
examples.english: You can feel the charm of bygone eras in the old townscape.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねるほどに{味|あじ}わいが{増|ま}す{俳優|はいゆう}だ。
examples.english: This actor gains more depth with each passing year.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{何度|なんど}{読|よ}んでも{新|あら}たな{味|あじ}わいを{発見|はっけん}できる。
examples.english: No matter how many times you read this novel, you can discover new depth.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{深|ふか}い{味|あじ}わい (deep flavor/richness)
・{独特|どくとく}の{味|あじ}わい (unique charm)
・{味|あじ}わいがある (have character/depth)
・{味|あじ}わい{深|ぶか}い (full of depth, richly flavored)

The nominalized form of the verb {味|あじ}わう (to savor). More evocative and literary than the simple noun {味|あじ} (taste). The figurative sense 2 is very common and suggests something that rewards careful, lingering appreciation.
